# dsh-two-pane-sidebar

A persistent **plugin rail** for DeepSeek Harness — it moves the
plugin navigation out of the main s

idebar into a slim column of its own, leaving the sidebar to do
one job: new session, workspaces, se

into a slim column of its own, leaving the sidebar to do
one job: new session, workspaces, sessions.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The rail is **data-driven**: it renders whatever is registered in the host's `sidebar.panellist`
slo

t (`{ id, order, label, component }`). Install a plugin that registers a navigation entry and it
sho
ws up here automatically — no code change, no configuration. Unregister it and it disappears.

This plugin is **client-only**. It installs no Host behaviour, makes no network requests, sends no
t

elemetry, and never touches your sessions or workspaces. Its entire state is one `localStorage`
key.
## Requirements

| Harness | DSH Desktop / Web **0.2.1-rc.2** (Windows, macOS, Linux) |
| Runtime | none — plain ESM,

no build step, no dependencies |
| Compatibility | declares `engines.dsh = ">=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0"`,

dependencies |
| Compatibility | declares `engines.dsh = ">=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0"`, see Compatibility |
## Install

Pick one. All three go through the Host's plugin manager, which writes the profile manifest, runs
`p
npm add`, and applies the bundle patch.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then **restart the app** (profile changes are not hot-reloaded) and reload the page.

> The spec is forwarded to `pnpm add`, so `file:` / `link:` local paths work too — that is how
> dev
elopment installs work.
## Use

- Click a row to open that plugin's panel; the active row is highlighted with a left bar.
- Hover a

row in the narrow rail for a themed tooltip.
- The arrow button at the bottom switches between **52

px (icons only)** and **208 px (icons +
labels)**. It is in the same place in both widths, so it nev

er jumps.
- The choice is stored in `localStorage["dsh.two-pane-sidebar.v2"]` and survives restarts.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` disables the width transition.

There is no mode to configure: the rail is always on, and the sidebar always keeps its own width
(wh

atever you last dragged it to). The rail reserves its space with a left padding on the frame, so
the
conversation column gives up 52 px — the sidebar does not shrink.
## Uninstall
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Or quit the app first, then delete the `dsh-two-pane-sidebar` line from
`~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/p

ackage.json` and its entry from `dsh.profile.bundles`. Verify before
editing: editing profile files

while the app is running can trip a hot-reload race in unrelated
built-in plugins.
Nothing is left behind except the `localStorage` key, which is inert.
## How it works
`client.js` is the whole thing (~670 lines, no dependencies):

1. registers a component into the host's frame-level `shell.overlay` slot;
2. locates the layout fra

me (`[data-shell-overlay]`.parentElement) and sets `padding-left` on it to
reserve the rail's column

`sidebar.panellist` through `slots.entriesOfSlot()`, subscribes to slot and locale changes,
and ren

ders one row per entry;
4. renders each entry's own icon component directly (the host only injects `

renderSlot` into entries
that declare children, which this one does not), behind an error boundary s
hides the now-duplicated navigation list inside the native sidebar with one CSS rule.
Every host interaction is guarded: a missing service, slot, or DOM node degrades the rail instead of

ion is guarded: a missing service, slot, or DOM node degrades the rail instead of
breaking app boot.
## Compatibility

This plugin deliberately depends on host internals, all of which can change between Harness
releases

his plugin deliberately depends on host internals, all of which can change between Harness
releases:
| Depends on | Used for |

| `shell.overlay` slot | mounting the rail |
| `sidebar.panellist` slot + entry shape `{id, order, l

abel, component}` | the rail's content |
| `[data-shell-overlay]` and its parent frame | reserving t

he column |
| `nav[class*="_panelList"]` (hashed class) | hiding the duplicated nav list |
| `[class

*="sidebarCol"]` / `[class*="_root"]` (hashed class) | following the active skin |
| `@deepseek-ai/d

sh-client-ui-primitives` → `Tooltip` | themed tooltips |
| `ctx.layout.selectPanel(id)` | opening a

mitives` → `Tooltip` | themed tooltips |
| `ctx.layout.selectPanel(id)` | opening a panel on click |

If an update breaks one of them the rail degrades or disappears; it does not corrupt data. The
check

list for re-verifying after a Harness upgrade is in
docs/troubleshooting.md.
## Known limits

- Not a native second view container: the rail lives in the overlay layer and reserves space with
pa

dding. There is no draggable splitter, and the rail has exactly two widths.
- The conversation colum

n loses 52 px; the host's `viewport < 1024` "narrow window" threshold
therefore triggers 52 px earli

er than before.
- A skin that paints somewhere other than the sidebar column's own element will not

be followed —
the rail falls back to the theme tokens for that skin.
- Icon components are rendered

directly and must only depend on `{ size, active }`; anything else
degrades to a neutral placeholder

and must only depend on `{ size, active }`; anything else
degrades to a neutral placeholder square.
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`link:` installs a symlink, so after that every edit to `client.js` is picked up by a page reload —
no build, no copy step. Locale metadata (`locale/*.json` `meta`) is read at boot and needs a restart
